# exception original date

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:exceptionOriginalDate`](gmeow-exceptionOriginalDate.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/exceptionOriginalDate>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/calendar`](../../slices/calendar.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The original date/time of the occurrence being excepted — the instance that would have been generated by the recurrence rule.

## Structure

**Property shape:** datatype property; [`gmeow:ScheduleException`](../classes/gmeow-ScheduleException.md) -> [`xsd:dateTime`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime); functional

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:exceptionOriginalDate`](gmeow-exceptionOriginalDate.md) from [`gmeow:ScheduleException`](../classes/gmeow-ScheduleException.md) to [`xsd:dateTime`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to identify WHICH generated occurrence an exception overrides, by the date/time the recurrence rule would have produced — the RFC 5545 RECURRENCE-ID anchor.

### Avoid when

- Avoid recording the new time here (that is the replacement event's own placement) and avoid an [xsd:date](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#date) literal — base-triple time is [xsd:dateTime](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime) (P3); functional, so one anchor date per exception.

### How to use

- Write the full [xsd:dateTime](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime) the rule would have generated, in the schedule's time zone; pair with [`gmeow:exceptionReplacementEvent`](gmeow-exceptionReplacementEvent.md) when the occurrence is moved rather than cancelled.

### Examples

- ex:standupSkip [`gmeow:exceptionOriginalDate`](gmeow-exceptionOriginalDate.md) "2026-06-19T09:00:00Z"^^[xsd:dateTime.](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime.)
